output.summary: Tall, branching tree native to the Sikkim Himalaya, Bhutan, Nepal, Malaysia, Indonesia and West Africa, with additional natural populations reported in China, Myanmar, Java and Sumatra. It stands on stilt-like roots and bears very long, finely toothed leaves. Its orange-red, cone-like ripe fruits are sweet and edible.
output.edibilityNote: The sweet ripe fruit is edible; fruit and seeds are eaten as food or medicine across much of its range.
